aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.description: Our history and the values that guide everything we do.
aboutPage.foundingNote: JCI Phnom Penh was established in 2010 and officially recognized in 2012.
aboutPage.historyBody1: JCI Phnom Penh was founded by a group of young professionals who believed Cambodia's next generation of leaders needed a space to practice leadership before they were handed it — through real community projects, not just theory.
aboutPage.historyBody2: Since then, the chapter has grown into a volunteer-run network running monthly general membership meetings, skills trainings, and community development projects across Phnom Penh and neighboring provinces, in partnership with local government, businesses, and the global JCI network of over 100 countries.
aboutPage.valuesSubtitle: Every JCI chapter in the world builds its projects and trainings around these four pillars.
aboutPage.valueBusinessBody: Skills training, networking, and mentorship for young entrepreneurs and professionals.
aboutPage.valueCommunityBody: Hands-on projects that address local needs — from clean water to disaster relief.
aboutPage.valueInternationalBody: Exchanges, partnerships, and friendships with JCI chapters across the globe.
aboutPage.valueIndividualBody: Leadership training that turns members into confident public speakers, project managers, and changemakers.

aboutCambodiaPage.title: JCI Cambodia
aboutCambodiaPage.description: The national organization connecting every local JCI chapter across the Kingdom.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyLead: JCI Cambodia is young compared to most JCI National Organizations, but it is proud, strong, and passionate about creating positive change in our community.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody2: JCI Cambodia was first created to bring together local business networks in Phnom Penh. After many trials and errors, the founding members learned that JCI's real strength is its like-minded members who want to learn to lead and grow.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody3: In 2010, Mr. Chy Sila, co-founder of CBM Corporation and Sabay Digital, helped register the association with the Ministry of Interior. JCI Cambodia became a Potential Member in 2010 and a Provisional Member in 2011. In 2012, under second National President Mr. Kouch Sokly, it became a fully affiliated JCI member at the World Congress in Taiwan.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody4: From fewer than 10 founders, JCI Cambodia now has over 200 members and 100 volunteers across seven local chapters, with more on the way.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody1: Efforts to start JCI in Cambodia began over 30 years ago but were stopped by war and instability. In 2007, two Cambodian students, Mr. Va Vireak and Mrs. Lay Kanika, were invited by JCI Japan to the Young Leader Summit, where they met the JCI World President and other National Presidents.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody2: In 2008, with Mrs. Lay Chanrasmey, Mr. Chhen Chandara, and Mr. Heng Samnang, they began setting up JCI Cambodia. The Asia Pacific Development Council (APDC) visited several times in 2008–2009 to run training and recruit business leaders.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody3: Mr. Chy Sila then led the push for official recognition from JCI and the Cambodian government, and in 2012 National President Mr. Kouch Sokly and his board made JCI Cambodia a fully affiliated JCI member.
aboutCambodiaPage.missionBody: To provide development opportunities that empower young people to create positive change.
aboutCambodiaPage.visionBody: To be the leading global network of young active citizens.
